title: Classical Greek theater (Aeschylus' Prometheus trilogy) gave rise to geometric and psychological perspective

tellings.quote: it was the first moment in history of recorded history that people were able to take the position of spectators at a theater sitting in different places on different nights.

plain: Ancient Greek theater, the Prometheus plays of the playwright Aeschylus, first let people sit as spectators in different seats on different nights, and the claim is that this gave rise to perspective, both in geometry and in the sense of a personal point of view. The philosopher Jason Jorjani makes the case himself, citing the psychologist Julian Jaynes and his book The Origin of Consciousness in the Breakdown of the Bicameral Mind, along with Jorjani's own book From Prometheus to Atlas.
